findings.asked: Estimate the mean from a grouped table and explain why it is an estimate.
findings.wentWrong: Very well done; a few used upper bounds instead of midpoints, and some rounded the mean or gave the group it fell in. 'We used midpoints' or 'exact values unknown' earned the explanation.
findings.rule: Midpoints, not bounds; never round the mean.

findings.asked: Mean from a grouped table; median class.
findings.wentWrong: Weaker candidates skipped midpoints or fx, or divided by the number of groups; rounding 125.x to 125 lost a mark.

findings.asked: Mean from a grouped table; median class.
findings.wentWrong: Improving; residual errors were the upper boundary instead of the midpoint, rounding, and dividing by 6 groups.
findings.rule: Sum of fx over sum of f.

findings.asked: Mean number of people per taxi from a bar chart.
findings.wentWrong: Most read the frequencies; few multiplied by the values to get 120 people and divided by 40 taxis; wrong divisions (40/10, 120/4) were common, and answers were not checked for sense.
findings.rule: A mean must sit inside the range of the data.

findings.asked: Estimated mean from a grouped table.
findings.wentWrong: Rounding to an integer, dividing by the number of groups, and bounds instead of midpoints all persisted; candidates should check the mean lies within the data.
findings.rule: Check: is the mean between the smallest and largest class?

findings.asked: Estimated mean from a grouped table.
findings.wentWrong: Rounding to 26 lost a mark; a few used bounds; some did not recognise the question and tried cumulative frequency or frequency density.
findings.rule: Recognise the standard method: midpoint x frequency.

ruleToRemember: Midpoint x frequency, add, divide by the total frequency (not the number of groups); do not round the mean; check it lies inside the data range.
aStarSignal: Extracting a frequency table from a chart or histogram before computing the mean, and sanity-checking the result.
